title: LIN 2.2A node (commander and responder)

regs.name: CFG
regs.desc: Bit timing (static while the bus is in use)

fields.desc: nominal bit time in clocks, at least 16 (2604: 19200 bit/s at 50 MHz)
1 = measure the bit time of each frame on its sync byte (responder without a crystal)

regs.name: HDR
regs.desc: Commander: writing an ID sends a header (break, sync, protected ID)

regs.name: PID
regs.desc: Header seen on the bus (own headers included); reading frees it

regs.name: RSP
regs.desc: This node's role in the next response, taken once a header has been seen; writing RSP2 commits it. Not written before the response starts: the frame is ignored

fdesc.rsp_data: data to publish, byte 0 in bits 7:0 (sent first)

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Subscribed response received with a good checksum; reading RX2 frees it

fdesc.rx_data: data bytes, byte 0 in bits 7:0, unused bytes 0

fields.desc: bit time of the current frame in clocks (measured with auto-baud)

irqs.name: SENT
irqs.desc: a published response was sent completely

irqs.name: ERR_BIT
irqs.desc: a sent bit read back wrong; the node stopped sending

irqs.name: ERR_SYNC
irqs.desc: break delimiter too long, or sync byte wrong or off-rate

irqs.name: ERR_FRAME
irqs.desc: dominant stop bit in the PID or the response

irqs.name: ERR_TIMEOUT
irqs.desc: subscribed response incomplete after 1.4 x its nominal length

notes: A commander writes HDR and also acts on its own header: it reads PID and writes RSP like any responder.
RSP can be written ahead: it is held (FLAGS.RSP_FULL) and taken by the next header.
